subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable auto-cleanup and archival policy for webhook/hook sessions

question: Should hook-agent sessions get a first-class cleanup/archive policy, and should it be hook-specific or part of a broader ephemeral-session model?
rationale: The missing behavior is source-proven, but the fix adds public config and can delete or preserve user transcripts, so automation should not choose the default mode or retention semantics without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add Explicit Hook Cleanup Policy
options.body: Add a `hooks.sessionCleanup`-style policy with conservative defaults, explicit transcript retention, and runtime handling for direct `/hooks/agent`, mapped hooks, and Gmail presets.

options.title: Use Existing Maintenance Only
options.body: Decline a hook-specific lifecycle knob and document that operators should use global `session.maintenance` for eventual hook-session pruning.

options.title: Design Broader Ephemeral Sessions
options.body: Fold hook cleanup into a wider cron/hook ephemeral-session model before adding public config surface.

recommendation.title: Add Explicit Hook Cleanup Policy
recommendation.body: Add a `hooks.sessionCleanup`-style policy with conservative defaults, explicit transcript retention, and runtime handling for direct `/hooks/agent`, mapped hooks, and Gmail presets.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter supplied the prior product-direction review on this issue, while the code history points to adjacent owners for implementation details.
